title: What numbers fill the blanks in this pattern of squares?
description: The video finds the rule behind three lines of squares and fills the blanks in the next two lines. It then adds the squares to check each line.
teaching_notes: One idea: in each line the third number is the first two multiplied, and the number on the right is one more than that. Watch for students who add the first two numbers instead of multiplying them.

video_script.why: The child finds the rule hidden in a pattern of squares, as in the solved example on odd numbers, and uses it to fill two lines.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the first two numbers to get the third, and add one to get the number on the right.
video_script.anchor: the three lines of the pattern with the next two lines and their blanks below
video_script.payoff_line: The blanks are twenty one, then ninety and ninety one

final_answer.spoken: the blanks are twenty one, then ninety and ninety one

never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: the slip: adding 9 + 10 = 19 fails on 2 + 3 = 5, not 6
video_script.design: One idea: multiply the first two, then add one for the right side. The pattern lines stay in the anchor band and the blanks fill in step by step.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three lines in the anchor band: 1² + 2² + 2² = 3², 2² + 3² + 6² = 7², 3² + 4² + 12² = 13²; two lines below with blanks: 4² + 5² + 20² = (__)² and 9² + 10² + (__)² = (__)²

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.lines: the three lines of the pattern appear one after another
marks.ask: the two lines with blanks appear below

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='lines'/>One squared plus two squared plus two squared is three squared. Two squared plus three squared plus six squared is seven squared.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Three squared plus four squared plus twelve squared is thirteen squared. What numbers fill the blanks in the next two lines?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the three blanks glow

marks.stop: the three blanks glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the first numbers 1, 2, 3 and the second numbers 2, 3, 4 lit in the three lines; the other numbers dim

marks.first: the first numbers one, two and three light up in the three lines
marks.second: the second numbers two, three and four light up
marks.step: an arrow shows each second number is one more than the first

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Look for a rule in the way the lines grow, as we did with the odd numbers. The first numbers go one, two, three.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second numbers go two, three, four.
<bookmark mark='step'/>The second number is always one more than the first.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, these three lines of squares are true.

marks.find: the two lines with blanks are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to fill the three blanks in the next two lines.

marks.one: 1 × 2 = 2 is written beside the first line
marks.two: 2 × 3 = 6 is written beside the second line
marks.three: 3 × 4 = 12 is written beside the third line

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, multiply the first two numbers in each line. One times two is two.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two times three is six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three times four is twelve. Each result is the third number of its line.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, the number on the right is one more than that result. Two and one make three.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Six and one make seven.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Twelve and one make thirteen. The rule fits all three lines.

marks.mult: 4 × 5 = 20 is written and matches the 20 in the line

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, take the first line. Four times five is twenty, which is the third number already given.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>One more than twenty is twenty one, so the blank is twenty one.

marks.mult: 9 × 10 = 90 fills the first blank of the second line

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step four, take the second line. Nine times ten is ninety, so ninety is the third number.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>One more than ninety is ninety one, so that is the number on the right.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step five, put the answers back in the question. Sixteen plus twenty five plus four hundred is four hundred forty one, which is twenty one squared.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second line is eighty one plus one hundred plus eight thousand one hundred. That is eight thousand two hundred eighty one, which is ninety one squared.

marks.ans: the three blanks are filled and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The blanks are twenty one, then ninety and ninety one.
